graph_source: Transition counts between successive concept answers; a separate dense graph is uniform
evidence_note: The transition graph sets A_ij to n_ij over the sum of n_ik, where n_ij is the number of times concept j was answered immediately after concept i. That section does not say the counts use the training split only. The dense graph in the same section is a uniform adjacency and is not a log statistic.
Edges are question-skill relations used for embedding propagation. The searched pages do not define those edges as co-occurrence, transition, session, or answer-similarity statistics.

The edge weight is the co-correctness rate among answered co-occurred exercises, kept when the rate exceeds a threshold. The phrase 'all the answered' does not say whether the counts include the test split.

graph_source: Exercise co-correctness and concept co-mastery subgraphs
evidence_note: The exercise and concept subgraphs are built from accumulated co-correctness and co-mastery rates over answered co-occurred pairs. No sentence restricts those counts to the training split.
The graph is the prerequisite structure between pedagogical concepts. It is not constructed as a statistic of interaction logs.

graph_source: Supplied prerequisite edges and supplied similarity triples
evidence_note: The Junyi graph is described with prerequisite pairs and similarity triples of the form (concept1, concept2, similarity value). The footnote treats similarity as content similarity. The paper does not compute those edges from answer logs.

A session graph is the partial order of (exercise, answer) tuples in an answering session. An 80/20 sentence elsewhere in the paper is the evaluation split, not a statement that the session graph excludes test interactions.
R is the binary adjacency between questions and skills. The sentence that difficulty is computed from the training dataset refers to the difficulty vector d, not to this edge set.

graph_source: Directed transition graph over learning sequences
evidence_note: The directed transition graph describes transitions between interactions according to the learning sequences of all students. 'All students' does not state that the graph was built on the unsplit dataset or on the training split only.
The knowledge structure is the prerequisite graph among pedagogical concepts. The text says those prerequisites are already given by experts.

graph_source: Latent-concept graph built from memory of the interaction sequence
evidence_note: The model dynamically constructs a graph of latent concepts from its memory of the interaction sequence. The remark on p.2 that other graphs are predefined on training-data ground truth refers to prior methods, not to a split statement for this graph.

graph_source: Heterogeneous graph generated from the exercise sequence
evidence_note: The basic graph BG = (V, E, lambda) is generated from the exercise sequence and contains question, knowledge, and learner nodes. No sentence says this graph uses only the training portion of the logs.

graph_source: Heterogeneous graph of exercise content, knowledge, and difficulty
evidence_note: The graph is built from exercise content, knowledge, and difficulty. The frequency count on p.5 is meta-path sampling used to choose aggregation neighbors. It is not a co-occurrence or transition adjacency, and it is not a train/full split statement.
The graph is a concept map whose edges are prerequisite relations among concepts.

A continuous-time dynamic question-answering graph is constructed from answering behavior. No sentence says that graph is built from the training split only or from the full dataset including the test split.

Questions that share a skill are the nodes of one hyperedge, and each skill is represented as a hyperedge. That is a skill/template schema. The co-occurrence sentence on the same page describes another model.

The paper states that a weighted heterogeneous graph is constructed according to the training data, with student, question, and skill nodes. The question-skill weight is the difficulty calculated in the training data.

The concept-question graph is produced by prompting GPT-4 to select related concepts from a list. The p.7 sentence that GKT extracts a transition graph from training data describes the GKT baseline, not SINKT's graph.
The heterogeneous graph has template, question, and skill nodes. The stated relations are Q to S, the question involves the skill, and Q to T, the question belongs to the template.

Students, questions, and concepts are placed in one graph, and a student-question link records that the student answered the question. The definition does not say those links are taken from the training split only.

graph_source: Knowledge-capsule graph and conceptual meta-path adjacency
evidence_note: A graph of knowledge capsules is used for latent prior relations, and a conceptual meta-path supplies the adjacency. The searched method pages do not define those edges as co-occurrence, transition, session, or answer-similarity statistics.
Problems and skills are two node types, and R-GCN propagates over problem-skill relevance. The searched pages do not define a log-count edge.

graph_source: Long- and short-term graphs instantiated on exercise records
evidence_note: The paper constructs graphs of concepts and exercises from the student's exercise records. On p.7 a short-term edge joins two exercises that share a concept, or two concepts that share an exercise. Neither page says those records are restricted to the training split.

A tripartite heterogeneous graph of concepts, questions, and students is constructed from the dataset. 'From the dataset' does not state that the construction includes the test split or is limited to the training split.

A reweighted logical-skills evolution graph is constructed from multiple submissions of the same problem. The 80/20 sentence on p.7 is the evaluation split. The grammar graph is a separate code-similarity structure.

Fig. 1 defines five associations: prerequisite and similarity links among questions, question-concept correlations, and prerequisite and similarity links among concepts. The method text updates association weights by attention on p.6 and does not state that the edges are counted from interaction logs.

The similarity adjacency is the sigmoid of I transpose I, and the dissimilarity adjacency is the all-ones matrix minus that similarity. The section does not say that I is formed from the training split only.

graph_source: Concept transition counts in the learning sequence
evidence_note: The relation strength is the count of concept j immediately following concept i, divided by the count of concept i, in the learning sequence. The equation does not say the counts are taken from the training sequences only.
Knowledge-aware and pattern-aware hyperedges are extracted from response sequences. No sentence says those sequences are the training split only.

graph_source: Interaction-derived question relations combined with a subject knowledge map
evidence_note: Question relations are extracted from historical learning interactions and then combined with a subject knowledge map. A cosine similarity on p.12 is a separate concept-concept weight. Neither passage states a train-only or full-data restriction for the interaction graph.
Edges are semantic dependencies derived from co-occurrence patterns of knowledge concepts in learners' response sequences. The page does not restrict those sequences to the training split.

The weight between two co-occurring exercises is the co-correctness rate among students who attempted both exercises. The equation does not say the attempts are limited to the training split. Wording that a related rate is computed in the dataset is not an explicit full-dataset statement.

For each practiced question, correct submissions with feedback Accepted are collected from the entire training data as its solution set, and similarity to that set is used by the code-graph adaptor. The learnable learner adjacency on p.4 is a separate matrix.

pypdf and pymupdf both return 0 characters, so the methods pages could not be searched. The file title and the expanded-corpus graph source identify an LLM-extracted knowledge graph, so this row is not coded as a log statistic.

Dynamic graphs are constructed from student responses. Nodes are previously attempted exercises or concepts, and edge attributes include attempt frequency. A training scheduler that selects a subset of the training dataset is not a statement that graph edges exclude test interactions.

graph_source: Collaboration and temporal edges, plus shared-concept edges
evidence_note: Collaboration edges link students who attempt the same question in a recent window, and temporal edges link consecutive interactions by the same student. Shared-concept edges are a separate relation. The page says the graph is updated as new data arrive and does not state a training-split restriction.
The bipartite graph connects questions to their associated concepts as defined by A. The searched pages do not add a co-occurrence, transition, or answer-similarity edge.

Temporal heterogeneous graphs are used to model interactive patterns among students, exercises, and skills. No sentence says this graph sequence is built from the training split only or from the unsplit dataset.

graph_source: Heterogeneous information network built from learning records
evidence_note: The figure caption states that a heterogeneous information network is constructed based on learning records, after which meta-paths form coarse and fine views. 'Based on learning records' does not say the records are the training split only. A 20/40/60 training-rate experiment is a reduced-data evaluation, not this construction split.

graph_source: Exercise-concept bipartite graph and intra-class relatedness graphs
evidence_note: G1 links an exercise to a concept when they are related. G2 and G3 set the relation to 1 when two exercises, or two concepts, are related. The searched pages do not give a formula that computes that relation from interaction logs.
